original_text: “We delivered solid performance across all five of our product categories in the first quarter, supported by our needs-based model and ongoing customer engagement. We continued to gain market share in farm and ranch and had strong double-digit growth in digital sales. Performance was led by companion animal, which outpaced the Company average, and we are taking decisive actions to improve its performance,” said Hal Lawton, President and Chief Executive Officer of Tractor Supply Company. Net sales for the first quarter of 2026 increased 3.6% to $3.59 billion from $3.47 billion in the first quarter of 2025, driven mainly by new store openings and, to a lesser extent, comparable-store sales growth. Comparable-store sales increased 0.5%, compared with a decline of 0.9% in the prior-year quarter. Comparable average ticket rose 1.6%, partially offset by a 3.0% decline in comparable transaction count, while digital sales posted strong double-digit growth. Gross margin was essentially unchanged at 36.2%, benefiting from disciplined product-cost management and the continued execution of an everyday-low-price strategy, offset by higher tariffs and delivery-related transportation costs. Despite the increase in sales and stable gross margin, operating income declined about 6% to $233.4 million, net income fell about 8% to $164.5 million, and diluted earnings per share decreased to $0.41 from $0.34.
